To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Gassmann equation is a good tool for fluid substitution.
Gassmann fluid substitutions are a very useful tool in seismic reservoir analysis, and that the formulation and implementation of the algorithm for the Gassman fluid substitutions is straightforward.

1) The Gassmann fluid substitutions can be formulated in a simple way, 2) The Gassman fluid substitution algorithm can be implemented in a simple way in Matlab (computer program), and 3) The Matlab code can be used to perform fluid substitution in a quick and easy way.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: • The Gassmann fluid equation is derived in detail, and the physical meaning of the equation is discussed.
the following issues: (1) the formulation and algorithm of Gassmann fluid replacement, (2) the matlab program for Gassmann fluid substitutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Gassmann equation is a very powerful and useful equation for fluid substitution in the case of a single porosity.
Gassmann fluid substitutions are not only valid in the low-frequency limit (as commonly stated), but also valid for the high-frequency range, provided the fluid and the rock properties are known.

the Gassmann equation is the most widely used and most robust equation for fluid substitution in the industry, but its application should be limited to the cases when the pore fluid pressure is equal to the hydrostatic pressure, and the pore space is filled with a single fluid phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(1) the Gassmann equation can be written in a simple form as: Ks = K0 + K0(1-2K0/K1)(Kf/K1-1) where Ks is the saturated bulk modulus, K0 is the dry bulk modulus, K1 is the dry shear modulus and Kf is the bulk modulus of the fluid.
the Gassmann equation is a linear equation for the fluid substitution.

(1) the fluid substitution is formulated in terms of the elastic moduli (bulk and shear moduli) and the density of the rock matrix and the pore fluid; (2) a numerical example of the Gassman fluid substitution is given for an example of sandstone; (3) a Matlab program for Gassmann fluid substitutions is developed; (4) an example of the Matlab program is given.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Gassmann’s fluid substitution is not a black box.
the Gassmann equation is a nonlinear equation and should be solved iteratively.
the fluid substitution should be performed in a consistent manner.
